  • N: [ahī?] | itpēšu || gana | luqbīka
  • T: [O my] sagacious [brother], come, let me tell you,
  • L: [ahī?] ← ahu I “brother (st. constr. ahi, OA ahu/ū”; itpēšu ← itpēšu I “expert, competent Bab. of god, king etc.”; gana ← gana I “come on”; luqbīka ← qabû II “to say, speak, command”

3

  • N: [ ... ] | litmunu || ... | karšukka

  • L: litmunu ← lemēnu I “to be(come) bad”; karšukka ← karšu I “m. & f. stomach, interior”

4

  • N: [anāku] | ša šumruṣu || kâša | ludlulka
  • T: [In …] most distressful, I will always sing your praises:
  • L: [anāku] ← anāku I “I”; ša ← ša I “who(m), which”; šumruṣu ← marāṣu I “to be(come) ill”; kâša ← kâšim I “to you (2 sg. pron.) Bab., NA”; ludlulka ← dalālu II “to praise”
  • Note: [RN432: 302] restores the missing beginning of the line as [aradka]. The restoration given here follows [RN2198: 146].

  • N: ahurrâkū-ma | zārûʾā || šīmatu | ubtil
  • T: I was the youngest child when fate carried off him who begot me,
  • L: ahurrâkū-ma ← ahurrû I “junior jB”; zārûʾā ← zārû I “Bab.”; šīmatu ← šīmtu I “st. constr. šīmti, occas. šimit what is fixed”; ubtil ← wabālu I “(cf. also babālu) to carry, bring”

  • N: agarinnu | ālittu || itâr | kurnūgi

  • Note: The reading of the last word follows the newly recovered fragment of the commentary @url{/fragmentarium/F.78}{F.78}, identified by T. Mitto. The metrical division of MS BabLB1 suggests parsing the line as nīš(i) ilīš(u)/iliš, “his oath” or “to/for/like an oath,” but this parsing would render the line impossibly difficult to understand. As taken here, the line refers to the king, who in choosing the sufferer would perform an action normally reserved to gods. Compare šarru šīr ilī šamšu ša nišīšu, “The king, incarnation of the gods, sun of his peoples” in Ludlul I 55. On the last line of the poem, see also the discussion in [dezorzi2024interplay], who argues that the poem constitutes a ring composition.
